data.summary: This response reports 2 overlays from 96 of 100 records; 1 of 1 inferential finding shows evidence at its alpha.
sentences: This response reports 2 overlays from 96 of 100 records; 1 of 1 inferential finding shows evidence at its alpha.
Overlay 1 (OVERLAY_T_CELL) `plan cells` runs 2 tests; 1 of them falls below alpha 0.05, unadjusted.
Overlay 2 (OVERLAY_ZSCORE_VS_TOTAL) `share` describes the host's values; it carries no p-value.
The run read 100 records; 96 passed the filters and 0 were left out for a missing value.
caveats: 2 p-values here carry no adjustment for multiple comparisons, so some may fall below alpha by chance alone; this is the concern the PULSE_ADVISORY_MANY_TESTS advisory raises.
Adding a multiplicity block (for example holm) adjusts them for multiple comparisons; then read p_adjusted beside each raw p-value.
OVERLAY_T_CELL carries no alpha of its own unless it is adjusted, so its p-values are read here against 0.05.

OVERLAY_T_CELL: Cells must use AGG_WELFORD, which supplies each cell's mean, variance and n. Without it the test uses one variance and n per side for every cell (params variance_target / variance_ref / sample_size_target / sample_size_ref, default variance 1 and n 2). Those p-values describe the values you supplied, not each cell's own spread, and they change with the measure's units.
OVERLAY_T_CELL: Target and reference are separate, independent samples. Equal variances are not assumed, and each mean should be roughly normal.
OVERLAY_T_CELL: The null hypothesis is equal means in the cell; the p-value is two-sided.

OVERLAY_T_CELL: Every cell is a separate test, so with many cells some small p-values turn up by luck; to adjust for multiple comparisons, set multiplicity on the overlay (holm or bonferroni hold the family-wise error, bh or by the false discovery rate) to add adjusted p-values beside the raw ones.
